basis: The printing heads this block 'VERS. 13-14.' and it opens 'VERS. 13, 14.-- At vero Mesraim genuit Ludim, et Anamim [ Z., Ananim], et Laabim,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Angelomus was a monk of Luxeuil in the middle of the ninth century and wrote for the Emperor Lothar I, who reigned from 840 to 855 and whom the verse prooemium addresses. The Genesis commentary is placed with his commentaries on Kings and on the Song of Songs in that decade. The wiki header gives the eleventh century, which is a century and a half out and is not followed. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1852 printing.
text: VERS. 13, 14.-- At vero Mesraim genuit Ludim, et Anamim [ Z., Ananim], et Laabim, Neptuim, et Petrosim, et Cesloim, de quibus egressi sunt Philistiim, et Capturim. Exceptis Laabim, a quibus Libyes postea nominati sunt, qui prius Futei vocabantur, et Cesloim, qui deinceps Philistiim appellati sunt, quos non corrupte Palaestinos dicimus, caeterae gentes sex ignotae sunt, quia bello Aethiopico subversae usque ad oblivionem praetentorum [ Z., praeteritorum] nominum. | Possederunt autem terram a Gaza usque ad extremos fines Aegypti.
